description: WE NAVIGATE MARS!!, or well, we help astronauts do so... but still, that makes us THE MARS NAVIGATORS!!
summary:
The Mars Navigators developed ARES-Gale, an astronaut-centric surface exploration and Extravehicular Activity (EVA) mission planning system tailored for Gale Crater and Mount Sharp. Navigating Mars poses extreme hazards: steep scarp slopes (>20°), rover-entombing Bagnold sand dune traps, severe diurnal thermal swings (−84°C to +4°C), cumulative cosmic radiation, and strict physiological life-support limits.

ARES-Gale bridges the gap between orbital data and human survival on the surface. Built with React, TypeScript, and high-performance WebGL, the system calculates multi-criteria traverse paths using authentic 50-meter NASA MOLA/HRSC elevation models. It models human locomotion speeds (Tobler formula) and metabolic energy expenditure (Minetti bioenergetics for a 130 kg suited astronaut). Furthermore, ARES-Gale dynamically tracks suit life support—including oxygen depletion from a 1000L tank, 4.2 kWh battery draw, and thermal load—alongside live in-situ weather telemetry from the Curiosity rover (Sol 4995 REMS and SwRI RAD dosimetry). By calculating a dynamic Point of No Return (PNR), ARES-Gale ensures astronauts maintain safe return margins, preventing wheel entrapment and life-support exhaustion.
details:
WHAT DOES IT DO OR HOW DOES IT WORK?

ARES-Gale is an operational surface tactical workstation designed for astronauts and flight controllers conducting EVAs in Gale Crater and Mount Sharp (Aeolis Mons). Users can select scientific destinations (such as Bradbury Landing, Rocknest, or custom map coordinates) to instantly generate multi-criteria traverse routes:

1. Balanced (P1): Optimizes between terrain safety and travel time.

2. Flattest (P2): Minimizes grade elevation gain for heavy cartage or rover driving.

3. Maximum Clearance (P3): Maximizes buffer distance from hazardous active dunes and cliffs.

The system samples 50-meter orbital Digital Elevation Models (DEM) from MOLA/HRSC to calculate true slopes, terrain contours, and vertical ascent. Using an adapted Tobler hyper-gravity function and the Minetti (2002) bioenergetics model for a 130 kg suited human under 0.376g Martian gravity, it calculates walking duration and metabolic energy (kcal and kJ). Simultaneously, it computes life-support draw on the 1000L suit oxygen supply and 4.2 kWh battery, coupled with Curiosity Sol 4995 REMS atmospheric pressure (777 Pa) and SwRI RAD radiation dose rates (24.2 µSv/h). It also offers a manual telemetry channel for crew EVA instrument check-ins and computes a dynamic Point of No Return (PNR).

WHAT BENEFITS DOES IT HAVE & WHAT IS THE INTENDED IMPACT?

- Astronaut Life Preservation: Eliminates catastrophic life-support exhaustion by establishing guaranteed 25% safety margins and a real-time PNR.

- Equipment Preservation: Protects surface rovers and crew boots from lethal wheel-slip traps in active sand dunes and insurmountable escarpments.

- Scientific Productivity: Maximizes sample return by routing crews safely across geological boundary units (clay-bearing Glen Torridon, sulfate layers, and Vera Rubin Ridge).

- Artemis & Mars Precursor: Serves as an open, deployable foundation for future pressurized rover operations and human-robot teaming on Mars.

WHAT TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES, HARDWARE, OR SOFTWARE DID YOU USE?

- Frontend: React 18, TypeScript, Vite.

- 3D Graphics & Simulation: Three.js, WebGL shaders for atmospheric entry flight and surface lander rendering.

- GIS & Vector Graphics: Custom reactive SVG cartographic engine with contour binning, elevation profiling, and any-angle smoothing.

- Mathematical Modeling: Python, Minetti bioenergetics, and Tobler locomotion equations.

- Cloud & Hosting: Vercel serverless edge deployment with GitHub CI/CD automation.

HOW IS YOUR PROJECT CREATIVE?

Rather than relying on static 2D satellite maps, ARES-Gale provides an immersive, mission-ready tactical workstation. It seamlessly bridges a cinematic 3D atmospheric descent with an interactive zoom dive into Gale Crater, merging real Martian geology with physiological bioenergetics. It is designed to feel like an authentic flight console an astronaut would interact with on a tablet inside a Mars surface habitat.

WHAT FACTORS DID YOUR TEAM CONSIDER?

- Martian Fractional Gravity (0.376g) and its effect on human locomotion efficiency.

- Suit Bulk & Mass (130 kg total system mass including xEMU portable life support).

- Thermal Barrier Dynamics (a 63°C temperature differential between internal 21°C suit climate and Martian ground frost).

- Sand Trafficability (avoiding active Bagnold dune slipfaces where rovers have historically bogged down).

- Point of No Return (PNR) limitations enforced by oxygen consumption rates and solar radiation limits.
